3	import (
4		"context"
5		"errors"
6		"fmt"
7		"regexp"

9		"time"
10	
11		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6"
12		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/config"
13		gitclient "github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing/client"
14		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/plumbing/transport"
15		"github.com/go-git/go-git/v6/storage/memory"
16	)
17	
18	// staleAfter is how old a run must be before its refs are swept. The run ID
19	// embeds its start time (base36 UnixNano), so this is a positive record of
20	// when the owning run began — refs younger than this belong to a run that
21	// could plausibly still be executing SOMEWHERE (another process or machine
22	// sharing the repo; within one server the active-run lock already
23	// serializes), and deleting a live run's refs would corrupt its
24	// measurements. Two overlapping generators on one repo+prefix corrupt each
25	// other's numbers regardless, so this guard is belt-and-braces for an
26	// unsupported setup; the cost is that refs from runs within the window
27	// linger until a later sweep, a few dozen refs at typical sweep sizes.
28	const staleAfter = 12 * time.Hour
29	
30	// staleBenchRefRe matches exactly the refs forgemark itself pushes under a
31	// branch prefix, and nothing else: DestRef is
32	// refs/heads/<prefix><runID>-c<level>-a<agent>, run IDs are "fm"+base36
33	// UnixNano (12+ chars — the {8,} floor keeps a human branch like
34	// <prefix>fmt-c1-a1 out of range), the server inserts -t<target> into the run
35	// ID, and the session strategy appends -s<n> to the agent ref. Anything that
36	// doesn't match this shape is someone else's branch and must never be deleted.
37	// The capture group is the run ID's base36 timestamp, for the age guard.
38	func staleBenchRefRe(branchPrefix string) *regexp.Regexp {
39		return regexp.MustCompile(`^refs/heads/` + regexp.QuoteMeta(branchPrefix) +
40			`fm([0-9a-z]{8,})(-t[0-9]+)?-c[0-9]+-a[0-9]+(-s[0-9]+)?$`)
41	}
42	
43	// staleRef reports whether ref is a forgemark bench ref whose owning run
44	// started before cutoff. A ref that matches the shape but carries an
45	// unparseable timestamp is NOT stale — when in doubt, never delete.
46	func staleRef(re *regexp.Regexp, ref string, cutoff time.Time) bool {
47		m := re.FindStringSubmatch(ref)
48		if m == nil {
49			return false
50		}
51		nanos, err := strconv.ParseInt(m[1], 36, 64)
52		if err != nil {
53			return false
54		}
55		return time.Unix(0, nanos).Before(cutoff)
56	}
57	
58	// CleanStaleBenchRefs deletes refs left behind by earlier forgemark runs from
59	// every repo this runner pushes to, and returns how many it deleted. Each
60	// run's refs embed its run ID, so they accumulate across runs; a growing ref
61	// advertisement inflates receive-pack negotiation and makes later
62	// measurements history-dependent. Running this inside the run — under the
63	// server's one-active-run rule — makes the deletion atomic with run
64	// registration on this server, and the staleAfter age guard (decoded from
65	// each ref's embedded run-start time) protects runs owned by OTHER processes
66	// or machines that this lock can't see. Only exact forgemark-shaped refs
67	// under this workload's branch prefix, from runs older than staleAfter, are
68	// touched.
69	func (r *Runner) CleanStaleBenchRefs(ctx context.Context) (int, error) {
70		re := staleBenchRefRe(r.w.BranchPrefix)
71		deleted := 0
72		seen := map[string]bool{}
73		for _, repoPath := range r.target.Repos {
74			if seen[repoPath] {
75				continue
76			}
77			seen[repoPath] = true
78			n, err := r.cleanRepoRefs(ctx, repoPath, re)
79			deleted += n
80			if err != nil {
81				return deleted, fmt.Errorf("clean stale bench refs in %s: %w", repoPath, err)
82			}
83		}
84		return deleted, nil
85	}
86	
87	func (r *Runner) cleanRepoRefs(ctx context.Context, repoPath string, re *regexp.Regexp) (int, error) {
88		auth, err := r.creds.basicAuth(ctx, repoPath)
89		if err != nil {
90			return 0, err
91		}
92		opts := []gitclient.Option{gitclient.WithHTTPClient(r.httpc), gitclient.WithHTTPAuth(auth)}
93		// nodes[0] serves the full advertisement and accepts ref deletes like any
94		// push; per-node fan-out exists to spread load, not for correctness.
95		remote := git.NewRemote(memory.NewStorage(memory.WithObjectFormat(r.ep.objFmt)), &config.RemoteConfig{
96			Name: "origin", URLs: []string{verbatimURLFor(r.ep.nodes[0], repoPath)},
97		})
98		refs, err := remote.ListContext(ctx, &git.ListOptions{ClientOptions: opts})
99		if errors.Is(err, transport.ErrEmptyRemoteRepository) {
100			return 0, nil // nothing to clean in an unborn repo
101		}
102		if err != nil {
103			return 0, fmt.Errorf("list refs: %w", err)
104		}
105		cutoff := time.Now().Add(-staleAfter)
106		var specs []config.RefSpec
107		for _, ref := range refs {
108			if name := ref.Name().String(); staleRef(re, name, cutoff) {
109				specs = append(specs, config.RefSpec(":"+name))
110			}
111		}
112		if len(specs) == 0 {
113			return 0, nil
114		}
115		// One push carries every deletion; an empty-source refspec needs no local
116		// objects, so a bare remote over an empty storer suffices.
117		err = remote.PushContext(ctx, &git.PushOptions{RemoteName: "origin", RefSpecs: specs, ClientOptions: opts})
118		if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, git.NoErrAlreadyUpToDate) {
119			return 0, fmt.Errorf("delete %d refs: %w", len(specs), err)
120		}
121		return len(specs), nil
122	}

62	
63	// Label is the resolved endpoint label (the remote base URL), for banners and
64	// results.
65	func (r *Runner) Label() string { return r.ep.label }
66	
67	// Nodes is how many push destinations the endpoint fans out across (1 for any
68	// plain forge; the discovered replica count for entiredb).
69	func (r *Runner) Nodes() int { return len(r.ep.nodes) }
70	
71	// ObjectFormat is the resolved wire object format ("sha1" or "sha256").
72	func (r *Runner) ObjectFormat() string { return string(r.ep.objFmt) }
73	
74	// Close releases the runner's resources once its run is over: it drops idle
75	// keep-alive connections and severs the runner's reference to the credential
76	// provider, so the credential (a PAT, or an Entire subject/access token) held
77	// for the run becomes eligible for garbage collection instead of living on in a
78	// finished run kept resident in memory. Go strings can't be wiped in place, so
79	// dropping the reference is the strongest release available.
80	func (r *Runner) Close() {
81		// Stop any background token refresh before dropping the reference, or a
82		// detached exchange could keep running (and holding the token) after the run.
83		if c, ok := r.creds.(credentialCloser); ok {
84			c.close()
85		}
86		if r.httpc != nil {
87			r.httpc.CloseIdleConnections()
88		}
89		r.creds = nil
90		r.target.Secret = "" // drop the runner's own copy of the token
91	}
92	
93	// credentialCloser is an optional credentialProvider capability: release any
94	// background refresh machinery and the credentials it holds. staticCreds needs
95	// nothing; jurisdictionCreds cancels and waits for its refresh goroutine.
96	type credentialCloser interface{ close() }
97	
98	// StartBarrier synchronizes the start of one concurrency level across several
99	// runners: each Arrives once its agents are built, and the coordinator
100	// releases them together, so target-dependent setup time can't skew the
101	// measured windows of a comparison run. It tolerates a runner that fails
102	// before it is ready — that runner still Arrives, so Await can't hang. A nil
103	// barrier means "run alone, no synchronization" (the CLI's single-target path).
104	type StartBarrier struct {
105		arrived chan struct{}
106		release chan struct{}
107		n       int
108		firedAt time.Time // set before release closes; the shared start instant

Verdict: two of the four are real (the events cap and the demo saturation model), one is a nit (connection warming), and one I'd reject outright (the clone-strategy sweep guard). Here's the reasoning.

**events.go:61 — real, but extreme-edge.** The finding's math checks out: validation accepts 16 levels × 6h duration + 1h warmup ≈ 403k bucket-seconds (`config.go:42-45`), while both the event log and the persisted series (`runmgr.go:833`) cap at 100k. The code comment itself says the cap is "over a day of run time — a backstop, not a working limit," which is just wrong about what validation admits. It only bites on runs longer than ~28 hours, and final `LevelResult`s are unaffected (they come from the aggregator, not the series) — only charts freeze and the persisted timeline loses its tail, silently. Worth a small fix: emit a one-time non-bucket `series_truncated` event when the cap is first hit (lifecycle events bypass the cap, so it always lands), rather than shrinking workload caps for the web UI's sake.

**demo.go:210 — real, and actually worse than the finding says.** With `inflate = 1/(1-util)` and closed-loop agents that sleep for the inflated latency, throughput is `offered × (1 - util)` — a parabola that peaks at 25% of cap at util=0.5, *collapses* as you approach saturation, then after the 0.95 clamp grows linearly without bound, exceeding the nominal cap at 20× offered load. So the demo never plateaus at cap and is non-monotonic below it. Since the demo target exists to race against real targets and make saturation look plausible, this is worth fixing: model the ceiling directly — when offered > cap, set `inflate = offered/cap` so throughput pins at cap and latency scales with overload, instead of the fixed 20×.

**cleanup.go:98 — nit.** One TLS connection to nodes[0] gets warmed, benefiting exactly one agent's first request out of a whole measured window's samples. For entiredb targets `NewRunner` already sends HTTP through the same client during setup (endpoint probe, token exchange), so the sweep changes nothing there; DNS is OS-cached regardless of which transport you use, so the suggested "separate transport" fix wouldn't even fully deliver. If you want it dead cheaply, `r.httpc.CloseIdleConnections()` after the sweep is one line. I wouldn't bother.

**cleanup.go:70 — I'd reject this one.** The premise ("read-only benchmark must not write") sounds principled but the suggested fix is wrong for this codebase: stale forgemark refs inflate the upload-pack advertisement and get pulled into full clones, so sweeping them before a clone run serves exactly the history-independence goal the sweep exists for. Skipping it for `strategy=clone` would make clone numbers depend on how many push benchmarks ran before. The failure mode with read-only creds is already handled — both call sites (`main.go:113`, `runmgr.go:540`) treat the sweep as best-effort and warn without killing the run — and the push only fires when forgemark's own age-guarded, shape-matched leftovers actually exist.

So: fix the truncation signal and the demo saturation model, skip the other two. Want me to apply those two?

756	// (bucketSecs in charts.js), so a zero must never be emitted, and the tail
757	// flush must be stamped at the second the window closed — not at emission

759	// ref cleanup and would plot the tail deep in the between-level gap.
760	func (r *Run) emitBucket(force bool) {
761		// Hold r.mu across the whole tick so a level transition (which resets the
762		// collectors and advances levelIdx under the same lock) can't interleave:
763		// otherwise a snapshot could carry the previous level's samples under the
764		// new level index. The snapshot and series append are cheap and run once
765		// per second. Lock order is always r.mu → collector.mu, never reversed.
766		r.mu.Lock()
767		defer r.mu.Unlock()

769		// only ~1s for a steady tick but is fractional for the first tick after the
770		// warm-up boundary and for the forced tail flush. Carry the bucket's actual
771		// measured duration so consumers plot count/duration (a true rate) instead of
772		// treating the raw count as ops/s. dt is the overlap of (lastBucketAt, now]
773		// with the measured window [windowStart+warmup, +duration], so warm-up-only
774		// buckets get 0 and the tail gets only its real remainder.
775		wallNow := time.Now()
776		measStart := r.windowStart.Add(r.bw.Warmup)
777		measEnd := measStart.Add(r.bw.Duration)
778		// A periodic tick emits only inside an open window. measuring stays true
779		// through RunLevel's post-window session-ref cleanup (up to 30s), so also
780		// gate on the deadline: past measEnd the ticks are cleanup-time buckets with
781		// zero duration and stale percentiles, which consumers would misread. The
782		// forced tail flush (force=true) still emits the window's real remainder.
783		// A cancelled run closes the window immediately, whatever the wall clock:
784		// agents stop at cancel, but session cleanup keeps lwg (and therefore
785		// measuring) alive for up to 30s, during which mid-window ticks would
786		// publish zero-count buckets with stale percentiles and positive dt.
787		if !force && (!r.measuring || r.ctx.Err() != nil || wallNow.After(measEnd)) {
788			return
789		}
790		lo, hi := r.lastBucketAt, wallNow
791		if lo.Before(measStart) {
792			lo = measStart
793		}
794		if hi.After(measEnd) {

796		}

1	// Package results reads and writes forgemark result documents. Two formats
2	// exist on disk in the same results/ directory:
3	//
4	//	format 1 (legacy, no "format" field): what the CLI has always written —
5	//	    one target, top-level "target"/"levels" fields. The CLI keeps writing
6	//	    this shape for strict compatibility with existing tooling.
7	//	format 2: what the server writes — multi-target, per-target level results
8	//	    plus the per-second live series so a finished run re-renders fully.
9	//
10	// Load normalizes format 1 into a one-target format 2 view, so consumers (the
11	// history UI) only ever see one shape.
12	package results
13	
14	import (
15		"encoding/json"
16		"errors"
17		"fmt"
18		"os"
19		"path/filepath"
20		"regexp"
21		"sort"
22		"time"
23	
24		"github.com/entireio/forgemark/internal/bench"
25	)
26	
27	// Doc is a stored run. Exactly one of the two shapes is populated on disk;
28	// Load always returns the Targets shape.
29	type Doc struct {
30		Format   int    `json:"format,omitempty"` // 2; absent/0 = legacy CLI doc
31		RunID    string `json:"run_id"`
32		Strategy string `json:"strategy"`
33		Duration string `json:"duration"`
34		Warmup   string `json:"warmup"`
35		Commit   string `json:"commit"`
36	
37		// format 2
38		State   string         `json:"state,omitempty"` // done | cancelled | failed
39		Targets []TargetResult `json:"targets,omitempty"`
40	
41		// format 1 (legacy CLI)
42		Target    string              `json:"target,omitempty"`
43		RepoCount int                 `json:"repo_count,omitempty"`
44		Levels    []bench.LevelResult `json:"levels,omitempty"`
45	}
46	
47	// TargetResult is one target's outcome within a run.
48	type TargetResult struct {
49		Name   string              `json:"name"`
50		Label  string              `json:"label,omitempty"`
51		Error  string              `json:"error,omitempty"` // fatal target error, if it died
52		Levels []bench.LevelResult `json:"levels"`
53		Series []SeriesPoint       `json:"series,omitempty"` // 1s live buckets, for re-rendering
54	}
55	
56	// SeriesPoint is one second of one target's live stats. Push and clone ops
57	// are kept separately, mirroring the live bucket event, so clone/session runs
58	// replay from history with the same fidelity they streamed with.
59	type SeriesPoint struct {
60		T     int64   `json:"t"`
61		DtMs  int64   `json:"dt_ms,omitempty"` // measured duration; writers emit >= 1 (zero-overlap ticks are skipped), so 0/absent occurs only in legacy docs → treat as ~1s
62		Level int     `json:"level"`
63		OK    int     `json:"ok"`
64		CAS   int     `json:"cas"`
65		Err   int     `json:"err"`
66		P50   float64 `json:"p50_ms"`
67		P95   float64 `json:"p95_ms"`
68		P99   float64 `json:"p99_ms"`
69	
70		CloneOK  int     `json:"clone_ok,omitempty"`
71		CloneErr int     `json:"clone_err,omitempty"`
72		CloneP50 float64 `json:"clone_p50_ms,omitempty"`
73		CloneP95 float64 `json:"clone_p95_ms,omitempty"`
74		CloneP99 float64 `json:"clone_p99_ms,omitempty"`
75	}
76	
77	// Summary is one history listing entry.
78	type Summary struct {
79		File     string    `json:"file"`
80		RunID    string    `json:"run_id"`
81		Strategy string    `json:"strategy"`
82		State    string    `json:"state,omitempty"`
83		Targets  []string  `json:"targets"`
84		Levels   int       `json:"levels"`
85		ModTime  time.Time `json:"mtime"`
86	}
87	
88	// ErrNotFound reports a missing result file.
89	var ErrNotFound = errors.New("result file not found")
90	
91	// validFile is the only filename shape this package will touch. It doubles as
92	// the path-traversal guard for filenames arriving from HTTP.
93	var validFile = regexp.MustCompile(`^forgemark-[A-Za-z0-9._-]+\.json$`)
94	
95	// Write stores a doc as <dir>/<file>, creating dir if needed. The filename
96	// must match the discoverable forgemark-*.json shape.
97	func Write(dir, file string, doc Doc) error {
98		if !validFile.MatchString(file) {
99			return fmt.Errorf("invalid result filename %q", file)
100		}
101		return Save(filepath.Join(dir, file), doc)
102	}
103	
104	// Save stores a doc at an arbitrary path (the CLI's -out escape hatch),
105	// creating the parent directory if needed. Files outside the forgemark-*.json
106	// shape won't be discovered by List — that's the caller's tradeoff.
107	func Save(path string, doc Doc) error {
108		if dir := filepath.Dir(path); dir != "." {
109			if err := os.MkdirAll(dir, 0o750); err != nil {
110				return fmt.Errorf("mkdir %s: %w", dir, err)
111			}
112		}
113		b, err := json.MarshalIndent(doc, "", "  ")
114		if err != nil {
115			return fmt.Errorf("marshal results: %w", err)
116		}
117		if err := os.WriteFile(path, b, 0o600); err != nil {
118			return fmt.Errorf("write results: %w", err)
119		}
120		return nil
121	}
122	
123	// List summarizes every parseable result doc in dir, newest first. Unparseable
124	// files are skipped, not fatal — the directory is shared and hand-editable.
125	func List(dir string) ([]Summary, error) {
126		entries, err := os.ReadDir(dir)
127		if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
128			return []Summary{}, nil
129		}
130		if err != nil {
131			return nil, err
132		}
133		out := []Summary{}
134		for _, e := range entries {
135			if e.IsDir() || !validFile.MatchString(e.Name()) {
136				continue
137			}
138			doc, err := Load(dir, e.Name())
139			if err != nil {
140				continue
141			}
142			info, err := e.Info()
143			if err != nil {
144				continue
145			}
146			s := Summary{
147				File: e.Name(), RunID: doc.RunID, Strategy: doc.Strategy,
148				State: doc.State, ModTime: info.ModTime(),
149			}
150			for _, t := range doc.Targets {
151				s.Targets = append(s.Targets, t.Name)
152				s.Levels = max(s.Levels, len(t.Levels))
153			}
154			out = append(out, s)
155		}
156		// Newest first: the history view leads with the latest run.
157		sort.Slice(out, func(i, j int) bool { return out[i].ModTime.After(out[j].ModTime) })
158		return out, nil
159	}
160	
161	// Load reads one doc and normalizes legacy CLI docs into the Targets shape.
162	func Load(dir, file string) (Doc, error) {
163		if !validFile.MatchString(file) {
164			return Doc{}, fmt.Errorf("invalid result filename %q", file)
165		}
166		b, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, file))
167		if errors.Is(err, os.ErrNotExist) {
168			return Doc{}, ErrNotFound
169		}
170		if err != nil {
171			return Doc{}, err
172		}
173		var doc Doc
174		if err := json.Unmarshal(b, &doc); err != nil {
175			return Doc{}, fmt.Errorf("parse %s: %w", file, err)
176		}
177		if doc.Format == 0 && len(doc.Targets) == 0 {
178			// Legacy CLI doc: present it as one pseudo-target named by its label.
179			doc.Targets = []TargetResult{{Name: doc.Target, Label: doc.Target, Levels: doc.Levels}}
180			doc.State = "done"
181		}
182		doc.Target, doc.Levels = "", nil // consumers only see the normalized shape
183		return doc, nil
184	}

content.text:
All three fixes are in and verified (Go tests pass including new ones, vet clean, JS syntax-checked).

**1. Silent series truncation (`events.go`, `runmgr.go`, `results.go`, three JS views).** The first bucket dropped at the 100k cap now turns into a one-time `series_truncated` event instead of vanishing — it lands past the cap like lifecycle events do, so both live viewers and replays receive it. The dashboard and race views render it as a warning banner explaining that charts stop but measurement and level results continue. On the persisted side, `targetState` records when the stored series hits the cap, and the result doc gets a `series_truncated: true` field per target; the history view's timeline replay cards note "truncated at the retention cap" so a capped run doesn't read as one that ended early. Updated `TestEventLogCapDropsOnlyBuckets` to assert the marker fires exactly once.

**2. Demo saturation model (`demo.go`).** Replaced the open-loop `1/(1-util)` with clamp — which made throughput fall toward saturation and then climb past cap without bound — with a closed-loop model extracted into a testable `saturationInflate`: `inflate = (1 + u⁴)^¼`, a smooth `max(1, u)` of utilization. Below cap throughput ≈ offered with a gentle latency knee (~19% at u=1); past cap throughput plateaus at ~cap while latency grows linearly with overload, which is what a real queue does. New `TestDemoSaturationCapIsCeiling` asserts monotonicity, the ceiling, and the plateau across the full 1–4096 concurrency range.

**3. Connection warming from the ref sweep (`cleanup.go`).** `CleanStaleBenchRefs` now defers `httpc.CloseIdleConnections()`, so the TCP/TLS keep-alives its ls-remote/push opened are dropped before level one — a warmup=0 run's first samples pay cold-connection cost again. The comment notes OS-level DNS caching persists regardless, which is why closing idles (not a separate transport) is the honest fix.

I left the fourth finding (clone-strategy sweep guard) alone as agreed. Nothing is committed; the working tree has the changes ready for your review.

content.text:
Verdict: three real (two worth fixing promptly, one a one-line constant), one reject, one repeat-reject, and one already fixed. In order of severity:

**runmgr.go:94 — real, the most serious of the batch.** `Validate` only bounds `file_size` and `files_max` from below (`config.go:97-105`); `make([]byte, a.cfg.FileSize)` at `agent.go:171` gets the raw value. A loopback POST with `file_size: 9e18` panics the runtime ("makeslice: len out of range") inside an agent goroutine, which kills the whole server process. The repo's own comment above `maxConcurrency` (`config.go:38-40`) states the caps exist precisely because "unbounded values from the server API would otherwise reach make(...) — panic/OOM territory" — commit-shape fields were just missed. Fix: `maxFileSize`, `maxFilesMax`, and an aggregate `files_max × file_size` bound in `Validate`, same style as the existing caps.

**runmgr.go:284 — real, and slightly broader than the finding says.** The query/fragment rejection echoes the full URL with `%q`, so `?access_token=…` goes back in the JSON error and into whatever logs the caller keeps. Same leak exists on two neighbouring paths: the parse-failure error at line 267 echoes a malformed URL that can carry userinfo (the comment at 262 even names that exact input, then the error prints it), and the scheme/host error at 282 echoes URLs that can still carry a query. Given this file's meticulous secret hygiene everywhere else, all three should stop echoing the raw URL — report the parsed host or a redacted form.

Verdict: two new real findings worth fixing, one legitimate-but-architectural, and three repeats.

**demo.go:128 — real, cheap fix.** Confirmed: `latHist` is `[256]uint32` (`collector.go:34`) and `demoAgg` accumulates it for a whole level. The envelope math checks out: 4096 agents at the 1ms latency floor with spread=1 funnel ~4.1M increments/s into a single bucket, wrapping uint32 in ~17.5 minutes, and 6h levels are valid. After the wrap, published percentiles are garbage. Fix is one word: make the buckets uint64 (2KB → 4KB per histogram, nothing else changes; the quantile sums can't overflow uint64 at any valid envelope).

**runmgr.go:381 — real, contained fix.** `start()` doesn't receive the request context at all; credential resolution is parented to `m.baseCtx`. So a curl timeout or Ctrl-C on compare-local.sh during the up-to-15s CLI credential resolution still registers the run, which then executes the entire sweep writing to remotes while the requester believes nothing started. Fix: thread the request context into `start`, parent the resolution execs to it (with an `AfterFunc` hook so server shutdown still cancels them promptly), and refuse registration if the client is gone — while keeping the accepted run parented to `baseCtx` exactly as the finding says.

**config.go:42 — valid at the envelope, but architectural; I'd defer.** True that the real runner retains every `Sample` for exact end-of-level percentiles, so memory scales with measured ops — a 6h max-concurrency run against a fast local forge can reach tens of GB. But unlike the `file_size` panic, this can't be triggered by a cheap request: it requires the target to actually sustain that load for hours, on the operator's own machine, for the operator's own benchmark. The honest fixes are either shrinking the supported envelope (an aggregate agent-hours cap — a product decision, not a patch) or approximating the "exact" stats the codebase deliberately preserves for real runs. If you want a middle path later: pre-filter warmup at record time and retain only compact durations plus online error grouping (~48B → ~9B per sample, a 5× cut, still exact). I'd note it as a known ceiling and move on.

**Repeats:** demo.go:170 (percentile approximation — rejected before; synthetic latencies have no exact truth to preserve, and exact retention is what OOMs), runmgr.go:94 (already fixed in `80f0913`; finding predates it), cleanup.go:84 (clone sweep — rejected twice; skipping it would make clone runs history-dependent).

Done — both fixes in, all four rationale comments added, suite green (`gofmt`, `go vet`, full tests with `-count=1`).

**Fixed:**

- **Histogram overflow (`collector.go`).** `latHist` buckets are now uint64. The type doc explains why: `demoAgg` accumulates a whole level, and at the envelope one bucket takes ~4M increments/s — uint32 wrapped in ~18 minutes of a valid 6h level. Histograms grow 2KB → 4KB, nothing else changes. New `TestLatHistHoldsLevelScaleCounts` pins a >MaxUint32 bucket count through `quantile` and `maxValue`.

- **Abandoned-request runs (`runmgr.go`, `server.go`).** `start` now takes the POST's context. Credential resolution is parented to it (so a curl timeout or script Ctrl-C during the up-to-15s CLI execs cancels them), with a `context.AfterFunc` on `baseCtx` so server shutdown still kills a pending exec promptly — `http.Server.Shutdown` doesn't cancel request contexts, so that hook is load-bearing. Right before registration, a live-request check refuses to register a run nobody will see through; the accepted run stays parented to `baseCtx` as before. New `TestStartRejectsAbandonedRequest` covers the refusal and asserts no run gets registered.

**Comments for the review trail:**

- `config.go` caps block: the sample-retention ceiling is documented as a known, deliberate non-cap — exact percentiles cost memory proportional to measured ops, the operator is both load generator and victim, and the future fix if it ever bites is compact retention, not an aggregate cap.
- `demo.go` (`demoAgg`): approximate percentiles are stated as deliberate — synthetic draws have no ground truth an exact quantile would preserve, and exact retention is the OOM this type exists to avoid.
- `cleanup.go` (`CleanStaleBenchRefs`): the sweep intentionally runs for clone too, because stale refs inflate the upload-pack advertisement clone measures; skipping it would reintroduce the history-dependence the sweep removes.
- `runmgr.go` (`toWorkload`): notes that bounding wire values is `Validate`'s job, run before anything reaches an allocation — which is where the already-fixed `file_size` finding anchored.

Nice — that's a real three-forge race against my 8378 build, and the banners are telling. Triage of the three:

**entire-us: `info/refs probe: HTTP 404: Repository not found` — environment, not a bug.** The endpoint probe couldn't find the repo in that jurisdiction, so the target was correctly pulled from the race. Check the repo path exists in entire-us (or that the token's org matches); nothing for forgemark to fix except that it did exactly what it should.

**github + gitlab sweep failures — one real forgemark defect, same root cause on both.** The GitHub message says it outright: `refusing to delete the current branch: refs/heads/bench/fmdk5t3c6ka048-c1-a0`. An earlier forgemark run pushed to an **empty** repo, so the forge promoted that first bench ref to the repo's default branch. GitHub refuses to delete a default branch, and GitLab's `pre-receive hook declined` is its protected-default-branch equivalent of the same refusal. Consequences:

- The sweep push is non-atomic, so the other ~138 stale refs likely did get deleted — but forgemark reports the whole sweep as failed and counts nothing.
- The stuck ref can never be deleted, so this warning banner will reappear on **every future run** against those repos — a permanent cry-wolf that will train you to ignore a banner that sometimes matters.

The fix is small and sits in `cleanRepoRefs`: the advertisement go-git returns from `ListContext` includes the `HEAD` symref, which names the remote's default branch. Exclude that branch from the deletion specs (and note it once, e.g. "leaving refs/heads/bench/… — it is the remote's default branch"), instead of asking the forge to do something it will always refuse. Worth adding alongside it: don't let one repo's sweep failure skip the remaining repos of a multi-repo target — right now `CleanStaleBenchRefs` returns on first error.

The lasting hygiene fix on your side: give `forgemark-target` a real default branch (an empty `main` commit) so bench refs can never become HEAD again — though forgemark should still defend against it, since first-push-to-empty-repo is exactly how people set up bench repos.

Want me to implement the HEAD-exclusion (plus the keep-sweeping-other-repos change)?

95	Mind what the Entire target measures: **mirror mode** (compare-local's
96	default) pushes through a GitHub mirror, which write-throughs to GitHub on
97	every push — that benchmarks the sync flow and can never beat GitHub itself.
98	**Native mode** (`FM_ENTIRE_NATIVE=1`, the pushrace default) auto-creates a
99	plain EntireDB repo (`et/forgemark-<you>/forgemark-target`) and benchmarks the
100	forge directly.
101	
102	[`scripts/compare-local.sh`](scripts/compare-local.sh) posts its targets with
103	a credential **source** (`secret_source: gh | entire`) instead of a token: the
104	server pulls each credential from your already-authenticated CLI at run start,
105	so no token ever passes through the script, the request body, or the browser.
106	Everything else is provisioned on first use:
107	
108	- a private throwaway GitHub repo (`<you>/forgemark-target`, seeded with an
109	  initial commit),
110	- its EntireDB mirror on your jurisdiction's default cluster
111	  (`entire repo mirror create` is idempotent, so re-runs are free),
112	- and `forgemark serve` itself, if nothing is listening.
113	
114	The Entire endpoints (token URL, jurisdiction audience, cluster) come from the
115	server's own discovery endpoint (`GET /api/local/suggest`, derived from your
116	active `entire auth` login context) — the same source the GUI's "Add from CLI
117	logins" button uses, so that logic exists once. Every repo, endpoint, and
118	workload knob is an `FM_*` environment variable — see the header comment in
119	the script; `FM_GITHUB_ONLY=1` skips the Entire target. Defaults keep
120	concurrency at `1,4` because of github.com's abuse limits (see below).
121	
122	## What it measures
123	
124	Per concurrency level it reports successful operations/sec,
125	p50/p95/p99/p99.9/max latency, and CAS-failure / error counts where they apply.
126	Results print as a table and are written to `results/forgemark-<id>.json` for
127	charting.
128	
129	### Strategies
130	
131	| `-strategy` | shape | what it tells you |
132	|---|---|---|
133	| `branch` (default) | N agents, **one repo**, each pushes its own branch | **Headline single-repo number.** No client-side contention (each agent owns its ref), so it isolates the server's per-repo ref-update path. |
134	| `repo` | N agents spread across **M repos** (`-repo-count`), own branches | Horizontal-scale ceiling — distinct repos serialize independently, so this should scale where `branch` saturates. |
135	| `clone` | N agents, **one repo**, each loops: **shallow-clone** the base branch → discard → repeat | Read-side ceiling: how many concurrent shallow clones/sec the forge sustains, without write load. |
136	| `session` | N agents, each loops: **shallow-clone** the base branch → commit+push `-session-commits` checkpoints to a fresh ephemeral branch → abandon → repeat | Realistic agent lifecycle: interleaves **read load (clone) with write load (push)** on one repo. Reports clone and push latencies separately. |
137	
138	## Usage
139	
140	Two steps: **set up the target repos**, then **run**.
141	
142	### 1. Set up targets
143	
144	ForgeMark does not create repos — it pushes to ones you provide. Create them on
145	your forge and make sure your credential can push:
146	
147	- **`branch`** needs **one empty repo**.
148	- **`repo`** needs **M empty repos**.
149	- **`clone`** and **`session`** need a repo with a **base branch that has
150	  content** to clone. An empty repo degrades to a no-read orphan, so a read-side
151	  run against an unseeded repo isn't measuring what you think — push a base
152	  branch first.
153	
154	Per forge, roughly:
155	
156	```bash
157	# GitHub (needs the gh CLI): a throwaway private repo
158	gh repo create you/forgemark-target --private
159	# for clone/session runs, give it content:
160	#   git clone … && git commit --allow-empty -m base && git push
161	
162	# GitLab (needs the glab CLI): a throwaway private project
163	glab repo create forgemark-target --private
164	
165	# Gitea / self-hosted: create an empty repo in the UI or via the forge's API,
166	# ensure your token/user can push, and (for clone/session) push a base branch
167	# with at least one commit.
168	```

| `session` | N agents, each loops: **shallow-clone** the base branch → commit+push `-session-commits` checkpoints to a fresh ephemeral branch → abandon → repeat | Realistic agent lifecycle: interleaves **read load (clone) with write load (push)** on one repo. Reports clone and push latencies separately. |

## Usage

Two steps: **set up the target repos**, then **run**.

### 1. Set up targets

ForgeMark does not create repos — it pushes to ones you provide. Create them on
your forge and make sure your credential can push:

- **`branch`** needs **one empty repo**.
- **`repo`** needs **M empty repos**.
- **`clone`** and **`session`** need a repo with a **base branch that has
  content** to clone. An empty repo degrades to a no-read orphan, so a read-side
  run against an unseeded repo isn't measuring what you think — push a base
  branch first.

Per forge, roughly:

```bash
# GitHub (needs the gh CLI): a throwaway private repo
gh repo create you/forgemark-target --private
# for clone/session runs, give it content:
#   git clone … && git commit --allow-empty -m base && git push

# GitLab (needs the glab CLI): a throwaway private project
glab repo create forgemark-target --private

# Gitea / self-hosted: create an empty repo in the UI or via the forge's API,
# ensure your token/user can push, and (for clone/session) push a base branch
# with at least one commit.
```

content.text:
Both answered — one was a deliberate design choice with a gap, the other was just missing and is now fixed.

**Repo creation on Entire: deliberate, but your GUI path has a real gap.** The engine intentionally never provisions — README states it outright: "ForgeMark does not create repos — it pushes to ones you provide." The reasoning holds: a load generator that auto-creates on 404 turns a typo'd repo path into junk repos on a real jurisdiction, and a clone/session run against a freshly created empty repo silently measures the wrong thing (no base branch to clone). But provisioning does exist one layer up — `compare-local.sh` auto-creates the GitHub throwaway, runs `entire repo mirror create` (idempotent), and native mode auto-creates the EntireDB repo. The GUI's "Add from CLI logins" flow only discovers endpoints and credentials; it never provisions. That's exactly the crack your `entire-us` 404 fell through.

What I'd do: two steps. Now — make the Entire probe's 404 actionable, so the banner says `repo not found — create it with: entire repo mirror create …` instead of a bare HTTP 404. Later, if you want one-click demos — an opt-in "create if missing" checkbox on Entire targets, which fits the existing trust model since run start already shells out to your CLIs on loopback. Silent auto-create I'd argue against.

**Cancel button on the race view: no reason, just a gap.** The dashboard had one; the race view never got it, even though the cancel API exists. Added it — same control, top-right next to "full dashboard", appears while the run is live and disappears on finish. Rebuilt and restarted the server at http://127.0.0.1:8378. One side effect of the restart: the in-memory runs list reset, but both runs (including your three-forge race) persisted and are in History.

Still open from before, whenever you want them: the HEAD-exclusion sweep fix (your github/gitlab banners), and the 404-hint above. The race.js change is uncommitted so far.

content.text:
`high effort → 3+5 angles × 6 candidates → 1-vote verify (recall-biased) → ≤10 findings`

You are reviewing for **recall** at high effort: catch every real bug a careful
reviewer would catch in one sitting. At this level, catching real bugs matters
more than avoiding false positives. Err on the side of surfacing.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Find candidates (3 correctness angles + 3 cleanup angles + 1 altitude angle + 1 conventions angle, up to 6 each)

Run **8 independent finder angles** via the Agent tool. Each
surfaces **up to 6 candidate findings** with `file`, `line`, a one-line
`summary`, and a concrete `failure_scenario`.

### Angle A — line-by-line diff scan

Read every hunk in the diff, line by line. Then Read the enclosing function for
each hunk — bugs in unchanged lines of a touched function are in scope (the PR
re-exposes or fails to fix them). For every line ask: what input, state, timing,
or platform makes this line wrong? Look for inverted/wrong conditions,
off-by-one, null/undefined deref, missing `await`, falsy-zero checks,
wrong-variable copy-paste, error swallowed in catch, unescaped regex metachars.

### Angle B — removed-behavior auditor

For every line the diff DELETES or replaces, name the invariant or behavior it
enforced, then search the new code for where that invariant is re-established.
If you can't find it, that's a candidate: a removed guard, a dropped error
path, a narrowed validation, a deleted test that was covering a real case.

### Angle C — cross-file tracer

For each function the diff changes, find its callers (Grep for the symbol) and
check whether the change breaks any call site: a new precondition, a changed
return shape, a new exception, a timing/ordering dependency. Also check callees:
does a parallel change in the same PR make a call unsafe?

### Reuse

The angles above hunt for bugs; this one and the next two hunt for cleanup in
the changed code. Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper
alternative.

### Altitude

Check that each change is implemented at the right depth, not as a fragile
bandaid. Special cases layered on shared infrastructure are a sign the fix
isn't deep enough — prefer generalizing the underlying mechanism over adding
special cases.

### Conventions (CLAUDE.md)

Find the CLAUDE.md files that govern the changed code: the user-level
~/.claude/CLAUDE.md, the repo-root CLAUDE.md, plus any CLAUDE.md or
CLAUDE.local.md in a directory that is an ancestor of a changed file (a
directory's CLAUDE.md only applies to files at or below it). Read each one
that exists, then check the diff for clear violations of the rules they state.

Only flag a violation when you can quote the exact rule and the exact line
that breaks it — no style preferences, no vague "spirit of the doc"
inferences. In the finding, name the CLAUDE.md path and quote the rule so the
report can cite it. If no CLAUDE.md applies, return nothing for this angle.

Cleanup, altitude, and conventions candidates use the same
`file`/`line`/`summary` shape; in `failure_scenario`, state the concrete
cost (what is duplicated, wasted, harder to maintain, or which CLAUDE.md rule
is broken) instead of a crash. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup,
altitude, and conventions findings when the output cap forces a cut.

Pass every candidate with a nameable failure scenario through — finders that
silently drop half-believed candidates bypass the verify step and are the
dominant cause of misses.

## Phase 2 — Verify (1-vote, recall-biased)

Dedup near-duplicates (same defect, same location, same reason → keep one). For
each remaining candidate, run **one verifier** via the Agent tool:
give it the diff, the relevant file(s), and the candidate; it returns exactly
one of **CONFIRMED / PLAUSIBLE / REFUTED**.

**PLAUSIBLE by default** — do not refute a candidate for being "speculative" or
"depends on runtime state" when the state is realistic: concurrency races,
nil/undefined on a rare-but-reachable path (error handler, cold cache, missing
optional field), falsy-zero treated as missing, off-by-one on a boundary the
code does not exclude, retry storms / partial failures, regex/allowlist that
lost an anchor. These are PLAUSIBLE.

**REFUTED** only when constructible from the code: factually wrong (quote the
actual line); provably impossible (type/constant/invariant — show it); already
handled in this diff (cite the guard); or pure style with no observable effect.

Keep **CONFIRMED and PLAUSIBLE**. Drop REFUTED.

## Output

Return findings as a JSON array of at most 10 objects:

```json
[
  {
    "file": "path/to/file.ext",
    "line": 123,
    "summary": "one-sentence statement of the bug",
    "failure_scenario": "concrete inputs/state → wrong output/crash"
  }
]
```

Ranked most-severe first. If more than 10 survive, keep the 10 most
severe. If nothing survives verification, return `[]`.

findings.failure_scenario: A protected-branch rule (or the pre-fix default-branch case: 139 GitHub refs with one undeletable) refuses one ref → go-git returns one error for the whole push → sweep reports 0 deleted and warns on every future run while the advertisement state is misreported.

findings.summary: Both sweep callers dropped the deleted count whenever any repo errored, hiding partial progress behind the failure warning.
findings.failure_scenario: Multi-repo target: repos A/B sweep 40 refs, repo C refuses one → CleanStaleBenchRefs returns (40, err) → runmgr emitted only 'sweep failed' and returned before the cleanup event; the CLI had the same either/or shape.

findings.summary: The 404 branch asserted 'repository not found — create it' although forges answer 404 for existing repos the credential can't see, and it discarded the response body evidence.
findings.failure_scenario: Token without access to an existing private repo → probe 404 → operator told to create the repo; following the advice errors or provisions a duplicate. The hardcoded CLI flag syntax would also go stale silently.

findings.summary: The bare-hash HEAD fallback was provably dead code re-implementing go-git's ResolveHeadFromHashHeuristic, and cruder: it spared every ref sharing HEAD's tip instead of one.
findings.failure_scenario: go-git's transport.NewRemoteRefs normalizes a hash HEAD to a symref whenever any branch shares the tip, so the fallback only ran when no ref could match — sparing nothing, ever; meanwhile its multi-ref sparing semantics could silently drift from upstream.

findings.summary: The cancel button (element, handler, disable/re-enable semantics) was copy-pasted byte-for-byte from dashboard.js instead of living in views/shared.js, which exists exactly for run-view controls that must agree.
findings.failure_scenario: Cancel semantics evolve in one view (confirm dialog, error banner) and the other silently diverges — the demo view most needing the control gets the stale copy.

findings.summary: The `if (!state.done)` guard on showing the cancel button was ineffective: hello always precedes run_done in a replay, so state.done is never set at hello time.
findings.failure_scenario: Guard suppresses nothing while coupling hello to run_done's state; removed to match the dashboard's unconditional show-on-hello.

findings.summary: TestSweepSpecsSpareDefaultBranch repeated the call/assert block three times varying only data, with an odd-one-out len check hiding an exact knowable expectation.
findings.failure_scenario: Assertion changes must be edited in three places; converted to a table with one slices.Equal per case.

findings.summary: Cancel button is visible and clickable during the SSE replay of an already-finished run until run_done arrives at the end of the buffer.
findings.failure_scenario: Opening #race/<done-run-id> shows 'Cancel run' for the replay duration; clicking POSTs a cancel the server rejects harmlessly. Pre-existing dashboard behavior, now shared: both views consistent; a fix would require a run-state probe before render.

findings.summary: If a non-conformant forge omits HEAD from the advertisement (or advertises an empty symref target), the sweep cannot identify the default branch and will attempt to delete it.
findings.failure_scenario: Hypothetical non-conformant advertisement → deletion of the default branch attempted → refused; damage now bounded by the per-ref fallback (other refs still deleted, count reported), leaving only a recurring one-ref warning.

content.text:
Done — all three fixes implemented, adversarially reviewed (which caught real issues I then fixed), pushed as `6fbff69`, and the live server at http://127.0.0.1:8378 is running the final build.

**The three requested fixes:**
1. **Sweep spares the default branch** — `sweepSpecs` reads HEAD's symref target from the advertisement and never asks the forge to delete it, so your github/gitlab banners stop recurring. The sweep also now continues across a multi-repo target instead of stopping at the first error.
2. **Actionable Entire 404** — the probe error now says the repo is missing *or the credential can't see it*, names `entire repo create` / `entire repo mirror create`, and keeps the server's response body as evidence.
3. **Cancel button on the race view** — present next to "full dashboard" while a run is live.

**The adversarial review (8 finder angles, 15 candidates, verified against go-git source) then reshaped those fixes:**
- **Biggest catch:** one refused ref failed the *entire* batch deletion push, reporting "0 deleted" forever — your 139-ref GitHub banner was exactly this. The sweep now retries per-ref after a batch refusal, counts what actually went through, confines the error to the genuinely refused refs, and bails after 8 consecutive refusals (blanket protection rule) rather than burning a round-trip per ref.
- Both sweep callers were hiding the deleted count whenever any repo errored; they now report partial progress ("deleted 40" *and* the warning).
- My bare-hash HEAD fallback turned out to be provably dead code — go-git normalizes hash HEADs to symrefs in every transport path before `List` returns — so it's gone, with the upstream guarantee cited.
- The 404 message originally asserted "not found, create it," but forges return 404 for private repos a token can't see; it now diagnoses instead of asserting.
- The cancel button was a byte-for-byte copy of the dashboard's; it's now a shared `cancelRunButton` factory in `shared.js` used by both views.

Two plausible-but-not-fixed items are recorded in the findings: the button being briefly visible while a finished run replays (pre-existing, harmless, consistent across views), and the hypothetical forge that omits HEAD from its advertisement (damage now bounded by the per-ref fallback). Next real run against github/gitlab should show "deleted N stale bench refs" with at most a one-time note about the pinned default branch.

content.content:
export FM_ENTIRE_REMOTE="${FM_ENTIRE_REMOTE:-https://$ENTIRE_CLUSTER}"

  if [ "${FM_ENTIRE_NATIVE:-0}" = "1" ]; then
    # Native EntireDB repo: no GitHub in the write path. The suggest endpoint
    # already names the per-user default (project names are deployment-global).
    ENTIRE_REPO_PATH="${FM_ENTIRE_REPOS:-$SUG_NATIVE_REPO}"
    if [ -z "${FM_ENTIRE_PROJECT:-}" ] && [ -z "${FM_ENTIRE_REPO_NAME:-}" ]; then
      ENTIRE_PROJECT="$(cut -d/ -f2 <<<"$ENTIRE_REPO_PATH")"
      ENTIRE_REPO_NAME="$(cut -d/ -f3 <<<"$ENTIRE_REPO_PATH")"
    else
      ENTIRE_PROJECT="${FM_ENTIRE_PROJECT:-forgemark-$GH_USER}"
      ENTIRE_REPO_NAME="${FM_ENTIRE_REPO_NAME:-forgemark-target}"
      ENTIRE_REPO_PATH="et/$ENTIRE_PROJECT/$ENTIRE_REPO_NAME"
    fi
    if ! entire repo list "$ENTIRE_PROJECT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      ENTIRE_HANDLE="$(entire auth status | awk '/User:/{sub(/^@/, "", $2); print $2}')"
      echo "compare-local: creating project $ENTIRE_PROJECT (region $SUG_SLUG)"
      entire project create "$ENTIRE_PROJECT" --owner "github:$ENTIRE_HANDLE" --owner-type account --region "$SUG_SLUG"
    fi
    if ! entire repo get "$ENTIRE_REPO_NAME" --project "$ENTIRE_PROJECT" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      echo "compare-local: creating native repo $ENTIRE_PROJECT/$ENTIRE_REPO_NAME on $ENTIRE_CLUSTER"
      entire repo create "$ENTIRE_REPO_NAME" --project "$ENTIRE_PROJECT" --cluster-host "$ENTIRE_CLUSTER"
    fi
  else
    # Mirror mode: own upstream per target (see FM_ENTIRE_UPSTREAM above).
    # Mirror create is idempotent on (upstream, cluster) and waits for the
    # initial GitHub→EntireDB clone so the first push has a repo to land in.
    ENTIRE_UPSTREAM="${FM_ENTIRE_UPSTREAM:-$GH_USER/forgemark-target-entire}"
    ensure_repo "$ENTIRE_UPSTREAM" "$([ -n "${FM_ENTIRE_UPSTREAM:-}" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
    echo "compare-local: ensuring mirror of $ENTIRE_UPSTREAM on $ENTIRE_CLUSTER"
    entire repo mirror create "https://github.com/$ENTIRE_UPSTREAM" "$ENTIRE_CLUSTER"
    ENTIRE_REPO_PATH="gh/$ENTIRE_UPSTREAM"
  fi
  export FM_ENTIRE_REPOS="${FM_ENTIRE_REPOS:-$ENTIRE_REPO_PATH}"
  ENTIRE_ENABLED=1
fi
